title: Bearing Shares on a Shortfall Behind a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
The share of what stands short on a Keyturn Host Payout Account that the host bears turns on where the loss behind it fell and on the protection plan in force under the host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment.

1. **Where the loss behind the shortfall was found to be the guest's fault and the protection enrolment in force is the Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan or the Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan**, the guest-at-fault bearing share of 80 percent applies.
2. **Where the loss behind the shortfall was found to be a third party's or no one's fault and the protection enrolment in force is the Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan or the Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan**, the shared bearing share of 90 percent applies.
3. **In every other case**, the host bears the whole of it, 100 percent.

The share is taken on what stands short, and the part the host bears is rounded half to even to two decimal places. What the protection enrolment carries is what stands short less that part, and it is not recovered from the host.

## Both parts of each case

Each of the first two cases requires both a finding on the loss and a plan. A loss found to be the guest's fault under the Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan meets the finding of the first case but not its plan, and falls to the third at 100 percent. A loss under the Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan whose finding is neither of those named falls to the third likewise.

## On hypothetical figures

Where what stands short is 500.00 USD: the host bears 400.00 USD in the first case and what the protection enrolment carries is 100.00 USD; the host bears 450.00 USD in the second and the enrolment carries 50.00 USD; and the host bears the whole 500.00 USD in the third, the enrolment carrying nothing.

The finding is the one carried on the most recent appraisal made under the enrolment, and the plan in force is the protection plan name the enrolment carries; both sit in the records of the Keyturn Host Protection Plan.
